expected_transcript:
Sit comfortably, supported by your chair or cushion. You may adjust at any time.

Notice sounds around you—the hum of the room, distant voices or quiet stillness. Feel the solid support beneath you.

Choose one familiar sound to return to, like the air conditioner or a clock’s soft tick. When your attention wanders, gently guide it back.

Return your attention to that sound now. Let it ground you in this moment, steady and present. Notice how it connects you to the space around you.

When other thoughts arise, simply return to the sound again. There is no need to control anything—just notice and come back.

Continue with the sound as your anchor. Trust yourself to return without instruction.

The chair beneath you remains steady. The sound continues around you.

Listen once more to the sounds here. When you’re ready, gently shift your hands or stretch your fingers. Open your eyes and return to your day.

limits: ASR is independent evidence, not a human transcription or a proof of perfect speech.
Noise rejection requires content agreement; duration and RMS do not prove speech.
Warmth, naturalness, voice identity, and quality require listener judgment.
Narration mode permits intentional silence; expected words still require recognition.
